object_types.name: Customer
object_types.definition: A person or organization that places orders in the system.

source_references.excerpt: A customer places an order.
Each customer has a unique customer ID in the CRM system.

I've heard some people call customers "clients" in the billing system. Are those the same thing? Good question. In our CRM they're "customers" but the billing team calls them "clients." For our purposes they're the same concept but the billing team has a slightly different definition -- they only consider someone a client once they've actually paid.

ambiguities.description: Definition of 'Client' vs 'Customer': The transcript indicates that 'Client' and 'Customer' refer to the same entity from the CRM perspective, but the billing team applies a stricter definition where someone is a 'client' only after payment. Should the model track this distinction (e.g., via a subtype or separate status), or treat all customers and clients as equivalent?

source_references.excerpt: I've heard some people call customers "clients" in the billing system. Are those the same thing? Good question. In our CRM they're "customers" but the billing team calls them "clients." For our purposes they're the same concept but the billing team has a slightly different definition -- they only consider someone a client once they've actually paid.

ambiguities.description: Optional participation in 'Order contains Product': The transcript states 'An order contains one or more products,' establishing that each order must have at least one product line. However, it does not explicitly state whether every product must appear in at least one order. Should a product be mandatory to any order, or can products exist in the catalog without ever being ordered?

source_references.excerpt: An order contains one or more products. Each line in the order specifies a product and a quantity. A product can appear in many different orders.

ambiguities.description: Frequency constraint on Order contains Product: The transcript states 'An order contains one or more products,' implying a minimum of 1 product per order. Should this be formally modeled as a frequency constraint (minimum 1, maximum unbounded) on the Order role, or is the mandatory constraint on the Product side sufficient?

ambiguities.description: Quantity as a role player vs. aggregation: The 'Order contains Product with Quantity' ternary fact type models Quantity as an attribute value of the order line. Is Quantity correctly modeled as a separate value type (implying it is always tracked), or could orders exist without specifying quantity in some cases?
